issues.detail: The Hebrew 'מִבְּלִי מֵשִׂים' means 'without anyone who understands/considers' (i.e., 'for lack of understanding'), but the Chinese renders it as '因無有永遠' ('because there is no eternity'), which misinterprets 'מֵשִׂים' (understanding/considering) as 'forever/eternity' (לָנֶצַח). This changes the meaning of the clause.
